chunks.text: We introduce a novel attention mechanism called Sparse Routing Attention (SRA) that reduces the quadratic cost of standard self-attention. Unlike dense attention, SRA routes tokens through a learned sparse gating network. Our method builds on the linear attention formulation of Katharopoulos et al. and extends it to encoder-decoder architectures.

The primary motivation for this work is the scalability bottleneck of transformers on long sequences. Existing approaches such as Reformer and Linformer reduce memory but sacrifice accuracy on retrieval tasks. We hypothesize that content-based routing preserves retrieval quality while maintaining sub-quadratic scaling.

We evaluate SRA on three benchmarks: LongBench for long-document QA, GLUE for general language understanding, and a custom retrieval corpus. On LongBench, SRA achieves 87.2 F1 compared to 82.1 for Linformer and 79.4 for Reformer, demonstrating that sparse routing maintains accuracy. However, our method underperforms on very short sequences where dense attention is already efficient.

expected_abstracts.statement: SRA achieves 87.2 F1 on LongBench, outperforming Linformer (82.1) and Reformer (79.4).
SRA underperforms dense attention on very short sequences.

chunks.text: Sparse Routing Attention consists of three components: a query projection layer, a learned gating function that selects top-k keys, and a weighted value aggregation. The gating function is trained jointly with the encoder via a straight-through estimator. This design requires no modifications to the decoder, making it plug-compatible with standard transformer implementations.

Prior work by Vaswani et al. established self-attention as the foundation of modern transformers. Subsequent research by Tay et al. surveyed efficient attention variants. Our approach contrasts with local-window attention methods because it uses global routing rather than fixed receptive fields. We also build on the routing principles of Content-Addressable Memory networks, adapting them to sequence modeling.
